functions.name: BlockProfile
functions.summary: BlockProfile returns n, the number of records in the current blocking profile. If len(p) >= n, BlockProfile copies the profile into p and returns n, true. If len(p) < n, BlockProfile does not change p and returns n, false.

functions.name: Breakpoint
functions.summary: Breakpoint executes a breakpoint trap.

functions.name: CPUProfile
functions.summary: CPUProfile panics. It formerly provided raw access to chunks of a pprof-format profile generated by the runtime. The details of generating that format have changed, so this functionality has been removed.

functions.name: Caller
functions.summary: Caller reports file and line number information about function invocations on the calling goroutine's stack. The argument skip is the number of stack frames to ascend, with 0 identifying the caller of Caller. (For historical reasons the meaning of skip differs between Caller and [Callers].) The return values report the program counter, the file name (using forward slashes as path separator, even on Windows), and the line number within the file of the corresponding call. The boolean ok is false if it was not possible to recover the information.

functions.name: Callers
functions.summary: Callers fills the slice pc with the return program counters of function invocations on the calling goroutine's stack. The argument skip is the number of stack frames to skip before recording in pc, with 0 identifying the frame for Callers itself and 1 identifying the caller of Callers. It returns the number of entries written to pc.

functions.name: CallersFrames
functions.summary: CallersFrames takes a slice of PC values returned by [Callers] and prepares to return function/file/line information. Do not change the slice until you are done with the [Frames].

functions.name: FuncForPC
functions.summary: FuncForPC returns a *[Func] describing the function that contains the given program counter address, or else nil.

functions.name: GC
functions.summary: GC runs a garbage collection and blocks the caller until the garbage collection is complete. It may also block the entire program.

functions.name: GOMAXPROCS
functions.summary: GOMAXPROCS sets the maximum number of CPUs that can be executing simultaneously and returns the previous setting. If n < 1, it does not change the current setting.

functions.name: GOROOT
functions.summary: GOROOT returns the root of the Go tree. It uses the GOROOT environment variable, if set at process start, or else the root used during the Go build.

warnings.message: Deprecated: The root used during the Go build will not be meaningful if the binary is copied to another machine. Use the system path to locate the “go” binary, and use “go env GOROOT” to find its GOROOT.

functions.name: Goexit
functions.summary: Goexit terminates the goroutine that calls it. No other goroutine is affected. Goexit runs all deferred calls before terminating the goroutine. Because Goexit is not a panic, any recover calls in those deferred functions will return nil.

functions.name: GoroutineProfile
functions.summary: GoroutineProfile returns n, the number of records in the active goroutine stack profile. If len(p) >= n, GoroutineProfile copies the profile into p and returns n, true. If len(p) < n, GoroutineProfile does not change p and returns n, false.

functions.name: Gosched
functions.summary: Gosched yields the processor, allowing other goroutines to run. It does not suspend the current goroutine, so execution resumes automatically.

functions.name: KeepAlive
functions.summary: KeepAlive marks its argument as currently reachable. This ensures that the object is not freed, and its finalizer is not run, before the point in the program where KeepAlive is called.

functions.name: LockOSThread
functions.summary: LockOSThread wires the calling goroutine to its current operating system thread. The calling goroutine will always execute in that thread, and no other goroutine will execute in it, until the calling goroutine has made as many calls to [UnlockOSThread] as to LockOSThread. If the calling goroutine exits without unlocking the thread, the thread will be terminated.

functions.name: MemProfile
functions.summary: MemProfile returns a profile of memory allocated and freed per allocation site.

functions.name: MutexProfile
functions.summary: MutexProfile returns n, the number of records in the current mutex profile. If len(p) >= n, MutexProfile copies the profile into p and returns n, true. Otherwise, MutexProfile does not change p, and returns n, false.

functions.name: NumCPU
functions.summary: NumCPU returns the number of logical CPUs usable by the current process.

functions.name: NumCgoCall
functions.summary: NumCgoCall returns the number of cgo calls made by the current process.

functions.name: NumGoroutine
functions.summary: NumGoroutine returns the number of goroutines that currently exist.

functions.name: ReadMemStats
functions.summary: ReadMemStats populates m with memory allocator statistics.

functions.name: ReadTrace
functions.summary: ReadTrace returns the next chunk of binary tracing data, blocking until data is available. If tracing is turned off and all the data accumulated while it was on has been returned, ReadTrace returns nil. The caller must copy the returned data before calling ReadTrace again. ReadTrace must be called from one goroutine at a time.

functions.name: SetBlockProfileRate
functions.summary: SetBlockProfileRate controls the fraction of goroutine blocking events that are reported in the blocking profile. The profiler aims to sample an average of one blocking event per rate nanoseconds spent blocked.

functions.name: SetCPUProfileRate
functions.summary: SetCPUProfileRate sets the CPU profiling rate to hz samples per second. If hz <= 0, SetCPUProfileRate turns off profiling. If the profiler is on, the rate cannot be changed without first turning it off.

functions.name: SetDefaultGOMAXPROCS
functions.summary: SetDefaultGOMAXPROCS updates the GOMAXPROCS setting to the runtime default, as described by [GOMAXPROCS], ignoring the GOMAXPROCS environment variable.

functions.name: SetFinalizer
functions.summary: SetFinalizer sets the finalizer associated with obj to the provided finalizer function. When the garbage collector finds an unreachable block with an associated finalizer, it clears the association and runs finalizer(obj) in a separate goroutine. This makes obj reachable again, but now without an associated finalizer. Assuming that SetFinalizer is not called again, the next time the garbage collector sees that obj is unreachable, it will free obj.

functions.name: SetMutexProfileFraction
functions.summary: SetMutexProfileFraction controls the fraction of mutex contention events that are reported in the mutex profile. On average 1/rate events are reported. The previous rate is returned.

functions.name: Stack
functions.summary: Stack formats a stack trace of the calling goroutine into buf and returns the number of bytes written to buf. If all is true, Stack formats stack traces of all other goroutines into buf after the trace for the current goroutine.

lines: pkg runtime, func Stack([]uint8, bool) int

functions.name: StartTrace
functions.summary: StartTrace enables tracing for the current process. While tracing, the data will be buffered and available via [ReadTrace]. StartTrace returns an error if tracing is already enabled. Most clients should use the [runtime/trace] package or the [testing] package's -test.trace flag instead of calling StartTrace directly.

functions.name: StopTrace
functions.summary: StopTrace stops tracing, if it was previously enabled. StopTrace only returns after all the reads for the trace have completed.

functions.name: ThreadCreateProfile
functions.summary: ThreadCreateProfile returns n, the number of records in the thread creation profile. If len(p) >= n, ThreadCreateProfile copies the profile into p and returns n, true. If len(p) < n, ThreadCreateProfile does not change p and returns n, false.

functions.name: UnlockOSThread
functions.summary: UnlockOSThread undoes an earlier call to LockOSThread. If this drops the number of active LockOSThread calls on the calling goroutine to zero, it unwires the calling goroutine from its fixed operating system thread. If there are no active LockOSThread calls, this is a no-op.

functions.name: Version
functions.summary: Version returns the Go tree's version string. It is either the commit hash and date at the time of the build or, when possible, a release tag like "go1.3".
